title: Breviary prayer (Pius V / Trent) addresses the Cross as distinct from Christ—‘O Cross … save the present throng’
source_text: XXI. Nam in Breviario Ecclesiae Romanae, juxta Synodi Tridentinae decretum restituto, & jussu Pii Papae V. in lucem edito, reperitur haec ad crucem a Christo distinctam directa precatio, O Crux splendidior cunctis astris, mundo celebris, hominibus multum amabilis, sanctior universis, quae sola fuisti digna portare talentum mundi, dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulcia ferens pondera, salva praesentem catervam in tuis hodie laudibus congregatam. In Festis Maii ad diem III. & in Festis Septembris ad diem XIV.
pass_a_gloss: For in the Breviary of the Roman Church, restored according to the decree of the Tridentine Synod and published by order of Pope Pius V, there is found this prayer directed to the cross as distinct from Christ: O Cross more splendid than all the stars, celebrated by the world, much beloved by men, holier than all, you who alone were worthy to bear the talent of the world, sweet wood, sweet nails, bearing sweet burdens, save the present throng gathered today in your praises. On the Feasts of May at day III and on the Feasts of September at day XIV.
pass_b_english: The restored Roman Breviary aims a feast prayer at the Cross as distinct from Christ: ‘O Cross … save the present throng.’
